title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

reports.title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

summary:
Angela Lipps, 50, of Tennessee is suing Fargo and police detective Lucas Heck for $10 million after being falsely charged with bank theft. She was arrested at gunpoint in July 2025 while babysitting four children, then spent about six months in jail, including nearly four months without bail awaiting extradition to North Dakota. Charges were dropped after her lawyer provided bank records proving she was in Tennessee when the fraud happened. She was released on Christmas Eve and later learned she had lost her home, car, and personal property.

The lawsuit says Fargo police relied on AI facial recognition that matched her social media photo to a fake ID used by a suspect, even though Lipps did not resemble the woman and had never been to North Dakota. It alleges Detective Heck requested an arrest warrant without enough probable cause and that the department lacked proper training and supervision for facial recognition tools. Fargo officials declined to comment on pending litigation. Lipps is seeking damages and accountability, hoping the case will make officers more careful with AI technology.
